# The Leadership Forge

> Practical AI professional development for K-12 district leaders, built by a practicing K-12 Director of Technology. The program ladders from AI Foundations through an AI Equity Audit into three tracks — Fluency, Strategy, and Action — and every course ends in a working artifact (governance framework, pilot design, board communication, 3-year roadmap) that leaders use in their districts.

## About the instructor

Mike Peck is a practicing K-12 Director of Technology. The Leadership Forge is built from the decisions actually sitting on a district leader's desk — not academic theory or vendor pitches. Every course scenario is drawn from real district work happening right now.

## Audience

Superintendents, assistant superintendents, principals, curriculum and instructional directors, and technology directors in U.S. K-12 public and independent schools. Resources inside each course are segmented by role so a principal and a tech director working through the same module each leave with deliverables for their own seat.

## The pathway

1. **The Launchpad (AI Foundations)** — Short orientation that establishes the shared language the rest of the pathway builds on. No technical background required.
2. **The AI Equity Audit** — Built into The Launchpad. A short structured assessment that scores a district across five categories (Fluency, Strategy, Action, Governance, Capacity) and routes the leader to the course that closes their largest gap.
3. **Fluency / Strategy / Action track** — Determined by audit results. Each track ends in a usable artifact for the leader's district.

## What the AI Equity Audit measures

The audit is a structured self-assessment scored across five categories. Each category surfaces a different aspect of district readiness:

- **Fluency** — How confidently leaders, teachers, and staff can use AI tools in their daily work.
- **Strategy** — Whether the district has a written, board-aligned AI strategy that connects to instructional and operational goals.
- **Action** — Whether AI use cases are moving from conversation into structured pilots with measurable outcomes.
- **Governance** — Whether acceptable-use, data-privacy, and equity policies cover AI specifically (not just generic IT).
- **Capacity** — Whether the district has the staffing, time, and PD infrastructure to sustain AI work over multiple years.

After completion, the audit produces a per-category score and a single recommended next course.

## Courses

- **The Launchpad** — Orients leaders to the AI landscape and runs them through the AI Equity Audit. Deliverable: a personal readiness profile and a recommended next course.
- **Command the Tools (Fluency track)** — Hands-on AI fluency for leaders who need to use the tools confidently themselves. Deliverable: a personal AI workflow.
- **Chart the Course (Strategy track)** — Building a board-ready 3-year AI strategic roadmap aligned to district priorities. Deliverable: a 3-year AI strategic roadmap.
- **Ship It (Action track)** — Designing and launching structured AI pilots with measurable outcomes. Deliverable: a pilot design document and board communication.

## Format

- Self-paced, four to five hours of focused work per course, broken into short modules.
- Typical leader finishes a course in two to three weeks at a module every few days.
- Every course issues a certificate of completion with documented hours.
- Aligned to ISTE and CoSN AI standards, but built around producing artifacts rather than awareness.

## Frequently asked

- **How is this different from ISTE or CoSN training?** ISTE and CoSN give standards and awareness — this program adds a system that ends each module in a usable artifact built for the leader's specific district.
- **Can I get PD credit?** Every course issues a certificate with documented hours. Whether those hours count toward state continuing-education requirements depends on the state and district; most leaders submit the certificate through local approval.
- **Is this only for tech directors?** No. It is built for the full district leadership team — superintendents, principals, curriculum directors, and technology directors. Course resources are role-segmented.
- **What if I'm new to AI?** Start with The Launchpad. No technical background is required anywhere in the pathway; this is leadership development, not technical training.
